scenes.headline: How Flide answers every question in one pass
scenes.sub: One shared state, many questions, one flat stream.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pavlo! A decision model scores options for many questions about one context. Here's how Flide runs them all at once, without changing an answer.

scenes.text: Lay the state and every question out as one flat stream, and fork the state so each question sees only the state and itself.
scenes.say: The idea: one stream for the state and every question, with the state forked so each question sees only the state and itself.

scenes.title: What a request costs
scenes.text: n x P + sum q   vs   P + sum q
scenes.say: A request is a state of P tokens and n questions.

parts.note: one sequence per question repeats the state
parts.say: Run each question as its own prompt, and the state is computed n times.

parts.note: compute the state once, then each question
parts.say: Share it, and the state is computed once. On long articles, that's over ten times fewer tokens.

scenes.title: Two ways engines share a state

left.title: A delimiter per question
left.say: Multi-item scoring shares the state, but each question reads an extra delimiter token, and its answer moves.

right.title: Flide's fork
right.say: Flide keeps every input exactly as it would be alone.

steps.say: Attention just needs a mask. But a gated delta net folds every token into one state, so a mask can't keep questions apart.
So each such layer runs twice. Call one reads every state and keeps its final snapshot.
Call two runs every question at once, each from its own request's snapshot, fetched by index.
The head reads each question's last token and scores its options.

steps.note: each question sees its state and itself
steps.say: In the paper's figure, each question lights up over its own state and its own block. Siblings stay dark.

scenes.label: faster than the best baseline, in one cell: Qwen3.5-0.8B, full QuALITY articles
scenes.say: The headline, nine and a half times, is one cell: the smallest model, long articles, about eighteen questions each.

scenes.title: Same workload, Flide's lead by model size
scenes.say: As the model grows, compute dominates and the lead shrinks. Small models gain most.

scenes.text: Keep the tree as metadata and run one stream: the state is computed once, and every answer stays its own.
scenes.say: Keep the tree as metadata, run one stream. The state is computed once, and every answer stays its own.

recap: Mask attention to state plus self
Fork the recurrent state by index
Gains are biggest on small models
scenes.say: Mask attention. Fork the recurrent state. Expect the biggest gains on small models.
